claims.statement: choose_sources must be called first and alone. It pauses on a card only when the person ticked nothing before sending; ticked sources arrive as AG-UI context, and TickedSources rewrites the model's choose_sources arguments to exactly those ticks, so no card shows.

choose_sources refuses (REFUSED with no artifact) staff spreadsheets for non-staff callers, Doc Vault files the caller cannot read or that are not in that org's vault, and a choice with nothing selected; staff paths are validated and registered as documents.

The run's allowed sources are read from the latest choose_sources ToolMessage: an artifact gives those Sources, an error status (rejected card) gives web-only, and no answer gives None. The answer lives only in the checkpointed messages.

Source choice is enforced on both sides: ChosenSources on the supervisor refuses every task call until choose_sources is answered (failing closed) and sets the CURRENT context variable per subagent, and RunSources, in the middleware of the entity-researcher, workbook-reader and vault-reader (not the catalog-writer), refuses any PULLING tool (web, library, staff workbook, vault) outside the choice; a subagent with no CURRENT reads nothing.

Web reads by the researcher are checked with check_url before the fetch and again on every redirect hop; a REFUSED reply is final, search results are marked READABLE or HELD, and read_page and fetch_document archive what they read to the source-archive bucket.

save_research refuses (returns REFUSED text) in four cases, in order: an NGO saved by a caller who is neither staff nor a steward (and, for a non-staff steward, an NGO not already held or not researchable by the caller via _may_research); fields with neither a finding nor a gap per research/contract.unanswered; a non-staff overwrite of another person's same-day row; and a save with fewer findings than the stored same-day row without replace=true.

A successful save_research upserts entity_research keyed on (slug, researched_on) in one transaction, then immediately publishes the brief; a staff-source save reports only the exception type on failure.

The brief is the record promotion reads: a markdown file at source-archive/entities/<slug>.md with no brief table, each fact carrying its typed finding in a hidden fact comment block and unplaceable facts in unplaced blocks, merged by fact_key across all research rows with the later run winning unless the earlier source is stronger by evidence tier then confidence.

Brief publishing is fail-safe: if Storage cannot be read, build raises and save_research logs and leaves the brief untouched while the findings stay saved; with Storage unconfigured the upload is a no-op and the reply points to make client-docs, so the phrase 'brief is published' only appears when it was.

Private (staff and vault) findings are excluded from the public brief, and a summary written from them is replaced by PRIVATE_NOTE; promotable adds the row's own private findings back only for promotion.

save_to_catalog (catalog/save.py) is the single save path used by both the Review screen route (POST /api/ingest/research/{slug}/save) and the catalog-writer's promote_research tool. It role-gates the caller (SaveRefused to 403 or REFUSED, LookupError to 404), reads the brief-merged research rows, then per organisation in one transaction runs undo.start, promote, _record_save and undo.finish, retrying once on UniqueViolation.

undo.start inserts a promotions row and sets sangam.promotion_id locally to turn on the write log; undo.finish clears it and deletes the promotion if catalog_writes has no entry for it, so a save that wrote nothing leaves no promotion and promotion_id is None.
After each organisation's save transaction commits, _publish_states writes each fact's end-state back into the brief; failure there is only logged because the catalog is already committed.

_record_save stores what a save wrote (with before/after row counts) on the entity_research row (saved, saved_at), the only record of what the profile held before since later plans read every row as same.

catalog-writer's promote_research is paused by SaveQuestions (ingest/middleware.py) on every call, carrying open questions, planned rows and coverage built by write_preview; only a person's edit can set decisions and model-written decisions are dropped. The writer's middleware also caps it at 12 model calls.

promote() (catalog/promote.py) applies source guards (pre-typed shape, staff-figure checks, vault and private-source holds) before the kind branch, and a funder promotion proceeds: resolve entity, write funder and tags, a documents row for every cited public source, CSR years, programmes parents-first, remaining facts in WRITE_ORDER, then document_links and the research link. Writes use fixed SQL through catalog/writer.py and Gate(plan=True) writes nothing.

Every fact ends in exactly one state (written, confirms, waiting, conflicts, kept, skipped, held, no column); unsettled in promote_records assigns held or no column to any fact no writer reached, and those states are written back into the brief.

undo.undo (catalog/undo.py; POST /api/ingest/promotions/{id}/undo, staff only) replays catalog_writes newest-first in one transaction, deleting inserts and restoring updates, only for the 19 LOGGED tables, and is all-or-nothing: UndoRefused (HTTP 409) if the promotion is already undone, a row changed since the save, or a row is now referenced elsewhere. Success stamps undone_at and resets the research to unsaved when no live save remains.
delete_research (DELETE /api/ingest/research/{slug}) removes research and vault findings only when no un-undone save of the slug stands, returning 409 otherwise.

Import tools run on the owner pool, so RLS does not apply; scope() supplies the run's caller (nobody outside a chat request) and each gated tool checks it itself: staff_only on staff-only tools, can_read_org on Doc Vault tools, and _may_save on the save path (a funder needs can_save_funder; an NGO must be held and researchable by the caller).

The Review screen path saves directly through ScreenReview posting decisions to the save route and treats a result with no entity as nothing saved; staff undo and delete are exposed through ResearchedRecently via the undo and delete endpoints.

ImportView loads all its panels with one GET /api/ingest/overview (to avoid cold-instance calls). For staff the overview includes sources, runs, queue and proposals; for other callers those are empty. Role access comes from accessOf, the screen uses NO_ACCESS until the overview answers, and Team tools render only for staff. After undo or delete only the research list is reloaded.

The research list is scoped to the caller: staff see everything; others see what they saved plus research on NGOs they steward, with private sources removed, a summary from private findings replaced by PRIVATE_NOTE, and promotion_id and saved_by blanked.

The overview's Doc Vault listing is best-effort: it lists up to 100 documents per membership org, keeps only private org documents, and on any failure logs a warning and returns an empty list so Import still opens.

GET /api/ingest/workbooks (staff only) lists .xlsx files for the spreadsheets card at the first pause and accepts only the staff-sources bucket (422 otherwise), matching the rule choose_sources applies to a pick.

A Doc Vault document is a documents row that is not public and whose storage_path is under the org-vault bucket. The vault-reader tools use the owner pool, so each checks can_read_org itself, returns the same answer for an unreadable and a missing file, and a run's picked org is the only vault it may list. Vault text sits only in the vault-reader, which has no web tools.

vault.read downloads up to 50 MB and reads PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, .md/.txt/.csv text files and png/jpg/jpeg/webp images (an image returned as itself, too-large ones reported). Text reads are capped at 24,000 characters, and every line is cited with [vault:<id>#p<page>], #para<n>, #slide<n>, #line<n>, #<sheet>!<cell> or #image markers; a scanned PDF is reported as having no text rather than guessed.

app/core/extract.py (which replaced ingest/office.py) is a pure bytes-to-text helper: docx_paragraphs returns paragraphs and table rows (a | b | c, merged cells once) in order, pptx_slides returns slide text, text_lines splits overlong lines, and xlsx_markdown renders each sheet's first 200 rows. It is used both for an upload's content_md (docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf; a damaged file leaves text None but keeps the hash) and by the vault reader for .docx, .pptx and text files.

save_vault_findings refuses the whole save, writing nothing, unless every finding has a vault source_url, cites a document in that org's vault and quotes its [vault:<id>#…] marker; NGO research also requires can_research_org. Findings go to vault_research (one row per slug, day and org), never into entity_research.

Vault findings are handled separately at promotion: research_rows (catalog/save.py) strips vault URLs from entity_research and adds vault_research findings only for a writer or person and only for orgs the caller can read; vault.hold_at_promote lets only a funder's general facts (PROMOTABLE concepts) through, holding the org's own facts and any NGO's vault findings.

Per docs/CHANGELOG.md 'Not finished', researcher-contract M5 (backfill KABIL and Axis on staging) is not done while M1-M4 (#194-#197) shipped; programme-themes step 5 write_funder_tags_from_programs (PR #172) is unmerged and no backend code defines it; the import-guided review follow-ups remain open; and Ask's SQL and Import still run on the owner pool, with the Ask fix on an unmerged branch.

run_import_now is in INTERRUPT_ON with approve and reject and no when condition, so every call pauses for a person whatever its sources value; it is the supervisor's one bulk write and is separate from the per-organisation research path.

run_import_now has an open-calls branch: after staff_only and the empty-goal check it tests tavily_news first, then funder_calls, before falling through to the adapter import. The funder_calls branch calls _calls_pull, which resolves named funders case-insensitively by name or slug, reports unknown names, returns 'nothing was read' if none resolve, reports other source keys as not run (a calls pull runs alone), and returns the report lines from calls.pull.run; failures come back as a string rather than raising.

The funder_calls pull bypasses the research path: the instructions have the supervisor call run_import_now(sources="funder_calls") straight away with no choose_sources and no researcher, relay totals and every NEEDS A LOOK line, and never research a call by hand when the pull was asked.
The Scout frontend treats news and calls tasks as pulls (isPull), so no sources step precedes them; the 'Check open calls' task card is offered only to staff and writes a lead-in into the composer.

ImportApproval reads the paused run_import_now arguments and Card picks a variant from sources: an open-calls card ('Check open calls?') when sources includes funder_calls, then the news card, else the generic import card. The calls card builds its funder and cost line locally (about 1 search and 2 small model calls per funder) with no plan endpoint, offers 'Check the calls' and "Don't check", and resolves with an approve or reject decision.

run_import_now, which carries the funder_calls open-calls pull, is one of the supervisor's own TOOLS (pipeline_tools adapter group) rather than a subagent tool; it runs without a task call, so ChosenSources (which guards only task) and subagent RunSources do not apply, and it is gated only by the INTERRUPT_ON approval and staff_only.

Once the researcher has called read_source_rows, StaffLastLock refuses every tool outside a small allowlist (OPEN_AFTER_STAFF) for the rest of the run, failing closed on unreadable state, so an injected instruction cannot carry a staff row out through a web URL or query.
